name: Residue-Conditioned Topological Admissibility (Refined)
statement: The recursive chain Delta -> R_↔ -> T -> A_adm -> delta_a -> Delta' governs lawful continuation update, while typed closure claims are evaluated through ↔_R rather than by collapsing residue into the closure operator.
formal_representation: A ↔_R B is true iff closure support remains admissible under A_adm

residue.definition: Process-generated trace that conditions future topology and admissibility.

residue_relation_operand.definition: The operand-level relation among residue conditions produced by lawful continuation.

residue_conditioned_closure.definition: A truth-valued closure relation holding only while admissible residue-conditioned topology preserves support between the operands.

topology.definition: The structural organization through which admissibility is evaluated.

admissibility_structure.definition: The admissibility organization conditioned by topology and residue.

corollaries.title: Admissibility Evolution
corollaries.statement: Admissibility is not a fixed law table external to process. Admissibility evolves through residue-conditioned topological organization generated by prior lawful continuation.
corollaries.interpretation: Future continuation legality may differ from past continuation legality even under similar local mismatch conditions.

corollaries.title: Decoupling Is Not Automatically Zero-State
corollaries.statement: Failure of a local typed closure claim A ↔_R B may produce exclusion or boundary-generation without forcing total collapse of process participation.
corollaries.formal_expression: (A ↔_R B) = True -> False does not by itself imply 0-state
corollaries.interpretation: Only failure of the primary core closure blocks all admissible continuation and triggers zero-state.

axiom_boundary_clarification.statement: The Primary Axiom remains invariant while admissibility structure evolves.

anti_reification_constraints: Residue is not an update operator
Residue conditions topology and admissibility only
R_↔ is residue-as-operand, not the closure operator
↔_R is closure-support-through-residue, not the residue state itself

decoupling_and_zero_state.decoupling_definition: Decoupling occurs when residue-conditioned support no longer preserves admissible closure between typed operands.
decoupling_conditions: nonzero distinction between operands is lost
closure topology cannot be preserved under allowed deformation
decoupling_and_zero_state.important_note: Local exclusion or boundary-generation is not automatically zero-state.
